verdict.justification: B provides the more defensible forecast by separating the year-end 2025 baseline from current 2026 published prices and using the latter to validate the recommendations. A explicitly acknowledges that its rates “already reflect 2026 carrier actions” but applies another estimated 2026 increase anyway, materially overstating the forecast despite preserving the carrier rankings. B also distinguishes USPS permanent prices, the temporary 8% increase, and holiday adders, whereas A uses holiday-period prices as the annual forecasting baseline. Both deliverables reproduce the shipment volumes and provide formula-based carrier-by-size cost comparisons, but B gives the shipping team more actionable guidance through UPS cubic-inch bands and a specific warning that an oversized Medium shipment can change the cheapest carrier. B addresses UPS surcharge treatment directly, while A leaves it unverified and recommends a potentially unnecessarily expensive FedEx fallback. Although B's recommendation cells are less dynamic than A's, its validation checks, clearer pricing chronology, and stronger operating guidance make it the preferable deliverable.

decisive_issues.issue: Applies an additional estimated 2026 increase to prices that already include 2026 increases.
decisive_issues.quote: Rates were retrieved 2026-11-05 and already reflect 2026 carrier actions; as instructed, the 2020-2025 average increase is still applied to estimate 2026 cost.

decisive_issues.issue: Uses temporary holiday-period USPS prices as the baseline for annual projected spending.
decisive_issues.quote: USPS prices include the temporary holiday peak-season increase (flat rate commercial +$0.85, Large +$1.75) effective Oct 4 2026 through Jan 17 2027

decisive_issues.issue: Leaves a material cost-comparison assumption unresolved.
decisive_issues.quote: Not verified: whether UPS fuel or residential surcharges are added to Simple Rate on top of the sheet price

decisive_issues.issue: Provides a concrete packaging-size exception that makes the recommendation safer to implement.
